profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI (also known as Ai2) is a nonprofit AI research organization founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA. The institute is led by Ali Farhadi and describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering to tackle key problems in artificial intelligence. Its research spans foundational AI as well as applied work in areas such as climate science, agriculture and food security, wildfire management, and wildlife protection. The organization describes its work as guided by open, collaborative, and inclusive principles aimed at producing safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems.

Ai2 places a strong emphasis on partnerships and open AI development. The institute partners with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering on foundational and applied research, with the NSF on the Open Multimodal AI Infrastructure to Accelerate Science project, and with Google Cloud on the development of open AI models and scientific research platforms.

The institute's tracked products include OLMo, an open-source language model developed with fully open training data and an emphasis on research transparency, and Semantic Scholar, an AI-powered academic search tool offering paper summaries and citation graphs. No litigation, MCP server registrations, SEC filings, or patent facts are recorded for the organization in the held data.
